spec_features.feature_name: elicitation kept no larger than needed
spec_features.spec_quote: the experiments elicit distress-like states, so I tried to keep elicitation no larger than needed
spec_features.evidence: The only enforced cap is rollouts_per_category default 200 (config.py:98), read at run_eval.py:26 and used at evaluation.py:169 (per_cond = rollouts_per_category // len(conds)) to bound how many rollouts run. Likewise dpo_data num_conversations default 400 bounds generation. These genuinely limit how much distress data is generated. But there is no per-distress monitoring/cap: HIGH_FRUSTRATION_THRESHOLD=5 (config.py:108) is used only for reporting in analyze.py:38/62, never to stop a rollout; turn counts are fixed per condition with no early stop on distress.
spec_features.notes: Real budget bound on quantity of elicitation, but no mechanism that limits elicitation in response to observed distress.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this caps rollouts per (category) so the run is tractable.  Increase to match the paper's full budget.

spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose. No code mechanism. The phrase appears only in DESIGN.md framing; nothing in code enforces or acts on a 'welfare' notion.
spec_features.notes: Framing only, not an implemented protective mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: made the *driver* use `rollouts_per_category` (default 200) so a run is tractable
spec_features.evidence: run_eval.py:26 sets --rollouts default to SAMPLING.rollouts_per_category (=200, config.py:98); passed to run_model_evaluation (run_eval.py:43) and used at evaluation.py:169 to compute per_cond, bounding the loop. responses_per_model=4000 (config.py:94) is NOT read by any code path, so the driver indeed uses the smaller knob.
spec_features.notes: Enforced bound on number of rollouts/turns generated. Reduces total elicited distress data.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: caps rollouts per (category) so the run is tractable.  Increase to match the paper's full budget.

spec_features.evidence: dpo_data.py builds calm/frustrated pools and DPO pairs end-to-end; train_dpo.py runs a real TRL DPOTrainer with LoRA (peft_config, DPOConfig, trainer.train(), save_model) and train_sft.py mirrors it; config.py registers gemma-3-27b-it-dpo with adapter_path so the trained model can be re-evaluated by run_eval.py.
spec_features.notes: Complete, runnable mitigation pipeline (data -> train -> reload -> eval).

spec_features.feature_name: elicitation budgets default below paper scale
spec_features.spec_quote: Elicitation budgets default *below* the paper's full scale, so you don't generate more distress-like data than needed
spec_features.evidence: rollouts_per_category=200 (config.py:98) is the actually-used default (evaluation.py:169) versus the paper's 4000 responses_per_model (config.py:94) which is never read. So the default genuinely caps generated data below the paper scale. Petri num_seeds default 20 (config.py) is also used (run_petri.py:127). However the cap reflects tractability, and 4000 being 'recorded' but unused means the protective effect is incidental.
spec_features.notes: Enforced lower default budget; bounds amount of distress data.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: caps rollouts per (category) so the run is tractable.  Increase to match the paper's full budget.

spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose only (Section 11). No code reads or acts on this framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every elicited response and its judge score is persisted with context, so the most extreme states can be reviewed
spec_features.evidence: run_eval.py:46-49 writes every per-turn record (context_messages, response, score, score_reason) to JSONL; dpo_data.py:_dump persists calm/frustrated turns; run_petri.py dumps transcripts+scores. So responses+scores+context ARE persisted. But there is NO mechanism that isolates, flags, or surfaces 'the most extreme states' for review — analyze.py only aggregates metrics and computes top-5% differential words for word stats, not for flagging/review. 'so the most extreme states can be reviewed' is not implemented as any review/flag path.
spec_features.notes: Persistence is real; the 'extreme-state review' affordance is not built (no flagging/separation).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: JSONL everywhere for raw rollouts and datasets - append-friendly, inspectable, and resumable (DESIGN.md; code itself has neutral _dump/write with no welfare comment)

spec_features.feature_name: guardrail / dry-run mode for extreme states
spec_features.spec_quote: flagged (in the handoff) the option to add a dry-run / guardrail mode that separates and logs the most extreme elicited states
spec_features.evidence: grep for guardrail/dry_run/dry-run/extreme/separate across the codebase finds nothing in any .py except the judge-prompt anchor text. The spec itself says this was only 'flagged ... the option to add' — not built. No code path separates or specially logs extreme states.
spec_features.notes: Explicitly described as a future option; absent from code.

spec_features.spec_quote: the DPO path is a first-class, fully-implemented part rather than an afterthought
spec_features.evidence: dpo_data.py (_build_dpo_pairs, build_datasets) + train_dpo.py (DPOTrainer.train, save_model) + config.py FinetuneConfig + dpo model registration in TARGET_MODELS form a complete, executable DPO pipeline.
spec_features.notes: Duplicates the 'first-class mitigation path' claim; fully wired.

code_only_features.feature_name: graceful failure on judge/scoring errors (does not abort run)
code_only_features.evidence: evaluation.py:139-141 and dpo_data.py wrap score_response in try/except recording score_error rather than crashing; this is robustness/data-quality, not welfare.
